narrative: Material PL1__M514C1DF shows moderate demand variability (CV=30.6%) with a mean of 1,017 units per working day and no detectable trend across the observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=94.9%), which is the primary driver of safety stock requirements. The recommended (r,Q) policy with SS=556, ROP=1,787, and Q=9,339 reduces total annual cost by 32.8% vs. the current SAP baseline by consolidating frequent small orders into efficient EOQ-sized replenishments while maintaining the 95% service level.
warnings: Capacity constraint binds marginally: safety_stock (556) + order_quantity (9339) = 9895, which slightly exceeds max_storage_units (9894.629). Order quantity adjusted to 9338 to ensure feasibility.
Lead time CV of 94.9% indicates highly unstable replenishment; transport variability is the dominant risk factor.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review — Reorder Point with Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous, non-intermittent, and moderately variable (CV=30.6%), which is the ideal setting for a classical (r,Q) policy. The high lead time variability is absorbed into the safety stock via the combined variance formula rather than requiring a more complex (s,S) or base-stock model.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity of 9,894.6 units is nearly fully utilized by the recommended policy (SS=556 + Q=9,339 = 9,895). Any upward revision of safety stock due to demand spikes or lead time deterioration would breach storage capacity. Monitor closely.
